name: Dairy & Meat Processing

objectives.text: Identify common dairy products made from milk such as cheese, butter, ice cream, and yogurt
Describe how milk moves from the dairy farm through the processing plant to the grocery store
Identify common meat products and the livestock species they come from, including beef, pork, lamb, and poultry
Compare the main steps used to process milk into dairy products and livestock into meat products
Describe useful by-products of meat and dairy processing such as hides, gelatin, tallow, and whey
Identify the primal cuts of beef, pork, and lamb and the carcass region each comes from
Explain the purpose of pasteurization and homogenization in fluid milk processing
Explain how milk is separated and standardized to produce whole, reduced-fat, and skim milk and cream
Describe how cream is churned into butter and how milk is coagulated and the curd separated from the whey to make cheese
Describe the steps of livestock harvest from humane handling and stunning through carcass chilling
Explain how the dairy and meat processing industries have developed from farm-scale production to modern processing plants
Describe the composition of milk and how its fat, protein, lactose, and solids content affect dairy product yield and quality
Identify retail cuts of beef, pork, and lamb by species, primal origin, and recommended cookery method
Explain how the conversion of muscle to meat, including rigor mortis and postmortem pH decline, affects tenderness, color, and water-holding capacity
Analyze how curing, smoking, and aging affect the flavor, color, and safety of a meat product
Explain how processed meats such as sausage and deli meats are formulated through grinding, emulsifying, stuffing, and cooking
Calculate dressing percentage and retail cutting yield from live, carcass, and retail product weights
Evaluate milk and dairy product quality using tests for somatic cell count, bacteria count, and off-flavors as practiced in the FFA Milk Quality and Products CDE
Apply sanitation, temperature control, and cold-chain procedures when handling, processing, and packaging meat or dairy products in the lab or an SAE
Explain the roles of USDA FSIS meat inspection and the Grade A Pasteurized Milk Ordinance in regulating meat and dairy plants
Evaluate beef and pork carcasses using USDA quality and yield grade factors such as marbling, maturity, ribeye area, and backfat as practiced in the FFA Meats Evaluation and Technology CDE
Develop a HACCP plan that identifies hazards, critical control points, and corrective actions for a dairy or meat processing operation
Construct standard operating procedures for a piece of meat or dairy processing equipment such as a grinder, slicer, or vat pasteurizer
Analyze current trends in dairy and meat processing such as plant-based alternatives, cell-cultured meat, and value-added products
Evaluate sustainability practices in dairy and meat processing such as whey utilization, by-product rendering, and water and energy use
Design a value-added dairy or meat product for an SAE or Agriscience Fair project, including formulation, processing steps, and quality checks

changes: Kept and reworded the six original competencies. The grade 12 quality control objective became a HACCP plan and a set of SOPs. Added foundational objectives on dairy and meat products, the farm-to-store path, by-products, primal and retail cuts, milk separation, butter and cheese making, and harvest steps. Added high school competencies on milk composition, muscle-to-meat conversion, sausage formulation, yield calculations, and cold-chain sanitation. Added milk quality and carcass grading aligned with the FFA CDEs, plus FSIS and PMO regulation, industry history, trends, sustainability, and a value-added SAE product. Left general preservation principles and fermentation science to the sibling sub-topics, and attached standards only to grade 9 to 12 objectives they actually teach.
